description: Russian (Cyrillic) phonetic transliteration convention actually used in the Bet-El app data. Default profile A = Sephardi/Edot-HaMizrach reading, strict 22-letter alphabet; profile B = Ben Ish Chai halacha bodies; profile S = prayers-ru.json patchwork. Everything below is derived from word-aligned (vocalized Hebrew, Russian) pairs; see RU-NOTES.md.

A.ruleModelAgreement: 95-99% word-exact with the rules below (torah 95.4%, tanya 95.9%, rambam 98.4%, zohar 97.4%, + qamatz-o leniency 1-2%; the rest = qamatz-katan, special words, word-initial dagesh, shva-nach doubts)

phonemeKeys: Hebrew letter/point NAMES (aleph, bet-dagesh, bet-rafe, kaf-sofit, qamatz-katan, shva-na, shva-nach, ...). Hebrew-side classification (dagesh qal vs chazak, shva na/nach, qamatz gadol/katan, mater vs consonant) is the core engine's job; this file only says what Cyrillic each class prints.

aleph.note: never written; only the vowel it carries is. No apostrophe/ъ for hiatus (e.g. йааков, веарец). Evidence: 170k words.

ayin.note: same as aleph (silent). Furtive patach under final ayin -> plain "а".

bet-rafe.note: profile B (Ben Ish Chai bodies) writes б: 2256 б vs 143 в on single-bet words.

gimel.note: plain г, no gh/ґ; he is ALSO г (see he).

he.note: he consonant (initial, medial, with vowel) = г: гашшамайим, гаарец, елогим, гу. he with shva-nach mid-word is г in 389 of 416 words (yigye, vegye) and silent in 27 (ехйе -> ейе, vейе, мамаг).

he-mappiq.note: final he with mappiq (ָהּ) = аг/ог: лаг, баг, отаг, лериштаг; 98% agreement.

he-mater-final.note: final silent he after qamatz/segol/tsere/cholam writes NOTHING (the vowel is already written): тора, зе, гине, моше. Profile B writes г after segol/tsere (зег 2246 vs зе 276, гарбег) but not after qamatz (а 6548).

vav-consonant.note: vav with its own vowel (and prefix vav-shva) = в: ве-, ва-, ваййомер; vav+vav doubled = вв (хиввар).

shuruk.note: vav with dagesh and no vowel = у, kubutz = у as well.

cholam-male.note: vav with cholam after a vowel-less consonant = о (no в).

chet.note: х, never кх/h/ch. Same letter as kaf-rafe.

yod-consonant.note: ALWAYS й + vowel (йа, йе, йи, йо, йу): never я/ю/ё/е-after-vowel. The letters я ю ё э ь ъ ч ж щ ы do not occur at all in profile A (inventory: абвгдезийклмнопрстуфхцш, 22 letters).

kaf-rafe.note: profile B: к 5494 vs х 386 on single-kaf words.

kaf-sofit.note: final khaf (ךְ / ךָ): мелех, ках, леха (A: 1009 х, 0 к); B: мелек, как.

lamed.note: always plain л - NEVER ль (профиль S / prayers-ru.json uses ль in 421 places: коль, аль, эль; A uses 0).

qof.note: к (same as kaf-dagesh); dagesh chazak -> кк.

tav.note: tav with or without dagesh = т (never с/th). Dagesh chazak -> тт (атта, битт).

qamatz.note: qamatz gadol = а. Qamatz katan = о (see qamatz-katan). Agreement 95.4% is entirely qamatz-katan words (кол).

qamatz-katan.note: Only detectable by the core (lexicon/syllable). Evidence: כָּל (every form) = кол in 100% of 7183+ occurrences in torah/zohar/tanya/rambam; qamatz before a letter with chataf-qamatz is katan = о (оголо, тогора, мимохорат, охора); корбан, мошзар, охло, дорхо. NOT uniform: חָכְמָה = хохма in torah-ru.json but хахма in zohar/tanya/rambam; vayyaqom-type (וַיָּקָם וַיָּמָת וַיָּשָׁב וַיָּרָץ) = ваййаком/ваййамот/ваййашов in torah-ru.json (102 words) but вайякам/вайямат with а in zohar (35 words).

chataf-qamatz.note: аголо, тогора, мимохорат; agreement vs a naive "а" is 29% because the preceding qamatz is katan (о) too: write chataf-qamatz = о and the preceding qamatz = о.

shva-na.note: Realised as е (never и/э/ъ). The Russian text agrees with true Hebrew syllabification; the core must decide na/nach.

torah-ru.json shva counts (shva written: word-initial incl. prefix ו ב ל כ מ ש and article ה
under a dagesh-chazak letter (הַמְּ הַגְּ -> гаммеорот, гаггедолим)
1053 е after patach, 383 after chirik (миббесари), 15 after segol
after short vowel patach/segol/chirik, closed syllable
silent: 4295 / 777 / 6822; е only 195 after patach (הַיְ: гайекум, гайеманит)
after qamatz / cholam / tsere / kubutz (written long vowel)
silent 785/362/181/73; е only 16/28/1 (identical letters וְגָלְלוּ вегалелу, רֹצְצוּ)
е in 1073, silent in 273 (the 273 are shvas after a quiescent aleph/ayin, e.g. מְלַאכְתּוֹ мелахто)

shva-nach.note: nothing is written; consonants cluster: яд-ха -> йадха, мишпахат, исраэль -> йисраел, берешит.

furtive-patach.note: ноах, руах, гароцеах, шама (ע: ганногеа, йегошуа). Profile B writes руха/ха-последним (641 ха vs 364 ах).

rules.rule: Output alphabet is exactly 22 Cyrillic letters а б в г д е з й и к л м н о п р с т у ф х ц ш plus hyphen. No ь ъ ы э ю я ё ж ч щ, no apostrophe/ъ for hiatus. All lower case except per capitalization rules.
rules.evidence: torah-ru.json char inventory (151k words) and zohar/tanya/rambam raw inventory: identical 22 letters.

rules.rule: Dagesh chazak doubles the Cyrillic consonant: гашшамайим, гаммайим, ваййомер, вайцавву, атта, шаббат, хаййим. Applies to every consonant with a Cyrillic letter (бб вв гг дд зз йй кк лл мм нн пп сс тт цц шш) and also yod/vav (йй, вв); NOT to aleph/ayin/he/chet/resh. Dagesh qal (begadkefat after shva or at word start or after a vowel-less cons.) does NOT double: мизбеах, ишто, берешит, увен.
rules.note: Profile B gemination rate ~93% (33189 expected, 30864 words contain any double letter) - noisy; S (prayers-ru.json) often omits it (шамаим, гамишпат, ихарету).

rules.rule: A dagesh on the first letter of a word that is a dagesh chazak by the previous word (e.g. לּוֹ לִּי נָּא זֹּאת) is doubled in torah-ru.json only ~42% of the time (121 doubled: лло, лли, нна, ззот; 166 single: ло, ли, на). Not predictable from the word alone.
Maqaf -> "-" ; each part is transliterated as its own word (shva at the start of the second part = word-initial shva-na): ал-пене, вайги-ерев, ашер-ло.
rules.evidence: torah: 11474 maqafs vs 11765 hyphens in torah-ru.json

rules.rule: Patach under final ח/ע/ה (after a vowel other than a, with no other vowel) is read BEFORE the consonant: ноах, руах, гароцеах, ганногеа, гаммизбеах.

Yod after chirik/tsere/segol with no vowel of its own is silent (the vowel is already written): йисраел, бене, елогеха, мицвотейха. Yod after patach/qamatz = й (ай): гаммайим, лай, ханай; after cholam = ой (гой); before final vav-shuruk the yod is й: вегайу; before final vav w/o vowel after qamatz the yod is silent and vav = в: алав, ехав, панав (ָיו -> ав, 978/978 in torah); ֵיהֶם -> егем (389/389).
rules.note: Profile B writes ָיו as айв (1005 айв vs 0 ав): алайв, мицотайв, гораотайв.

rules.rule: Vav+dagesh (no vowel) = у; vav+cholam (after vowelless cons.) = о; vav with a vowel = в+vowel; vav-dagesh with vowel (ּוַ) = вв.

Final he without mappiq, after a vowel, is silent (the vowel letter is already written): тора, зе, гине, моше. With mappiq it is г: лаг, баг, отаг. Any he that is a real consonant (initial/medial/with a vowel, or in הוּא) is г: гу, гем, гаарец, гашем.

Cantillation marks, meteg, sof-pasuk, paseq and the geresh/gershayim in abbreviations are ignored for the phonemes. Torah verse text carries NO punctuation at all in torah-ru.json; Zohar/Tanya/Rambam copy the source punctuation (, . : ( ) " -) at the same positions.

The FIRST word of each verse/paragraph/unit is capitalised (torah-ru.json: 5846/5846 verses; zohar 17078/17780 units; tanya 1596/1623; rambam 15070/15131). Mid-sentence capitals: ONLY the divine name Адонай (tetragrammaton / יְיָ), and a few titles (Рабби, Раши, Гаширим). Proper names (аврагам, йааков, йицхак, моше, давид, мицрайим), елогим, тора, шаббат are lower-case. אֲדֹנָי (real Adonai) is lower-case адонай (15) except verse-initial.

Source abbreviations are expanded, not transliterated: וְגוֹ / וְגו -> вегомер ; וְכוּ / וכו -> вехулеи ; ה׳ / יי -> Адонай. Hebrew numeral ג׳ / כב inside references becomes arabic digits (3, 22). Book names in references are Russian-translated (Вайикра 22 9), not transliterated.

Ben Ish Chai halacha bodies (data/chok-benishchai/*/*.ru.json, 122k words) are a different, noisier dialect: fricative begadkefat are written as stops (в->б: абал, дабар, тоб; х->к: как, мелек, беток, царик; ф->п: шопек, упаам), final he -> г (зег, марег, гарбег), ָיו -> айв, furtive ах -> ха (руха), gemination mostly kept (~93%), abbreviations end in apostrophe (гак', веку' 347x), word-for-word inconsistent within one paragraph (шеккатаб / шекатав, гиннег / гине, ейн / ен). Only 70-76% of B words equal the A-rule output, per-file spread tiny (0.63-0.76), i.e. uniform noise rather than sub-dialects.

data/prayers-ru.json is a patchwork: older keys (omerKavanot, omerClosing, talitTefilin, tikunChatzot ...) follow A (84-100%), newer/Tanakh-quoting keys (kaveh, aleinuShemaLine, hannahPrayer, einKeElokeinu...) use ь я э ё ѓ: эль, аль, коль, исраэль, Элоѓейну, веэт, Адонай; elogim/элогим 157 vs 220 елогим; барух 21 vs барук 36; ал 405 vs аль 253.

ה׳.count: inferred from prefixed forms; bare ה׳ not aligned in the corpus

לַה.count: 57 tanya, 11 rambam (ל + ה׳ abbreviation); בַּה -> баадонай 9 tanya; לָהּ with mappiq = лаг (1511 rambam)
לַה.note: ambiguous with לָהּ, decided by the points (patach+no mappiq = Adonai)

שַׁבָּת.note: regular, gemination (profile B: шабат 186 vs шаббат 1136)

הַשֵּׁם.note: regular (BIC 31x гашем, 9 Хашем, 85 Б-г are translated-text forms not transliteration)

corpus: scripts/translit/corpus-ru.json (dialect field A/B/S; ru is lower-cased for non-torah sources because capitalisation is a separate rule)
openQuestions: Which profile should the new text (Shulchan Aruch HaRav / sa-harav, a halacha text) follow: A (strict, 98-99% consistent, covers Torah/Zohar/Tanya/Rambam) or B (Ben Ish Chai halacha bodies, the closest genre)? Default A; needs owner decision.

Word-initial dagesh that is chazak because of the PREVIOUS word (לּוֹ לִּי נָּא זֹּאת בּוֹ): torah-ru.json doubles it in 121 words and does not in 166+ (begadkefat: 29 doubled vs 11075 single). The core cannot see it without the previous word; decide whether to implement dehiq/ve-hebdel context or never double word-initial dagesh.

Qamatz-katan: besides כָּל (100% о) and qamatz-before-chataf-qamatz, the sources disagree (חָכְמָה хохма in torah-ru.json vs хахма elsewhere; וַיָּקָם-type ваййаком in torah-ru.json vs вайякам in zohar). Sa-harav text has no U+05C7 marks, so a lexicon/rule list is required.

He with shva-nach mid-word (אֶהְיֶה, וֶהְיֵה, תַּהְפֻּכֹת, מַהְפֵּכַת, הִתְמַהְמֵהַּ): silent in 27 words (ейе, вейе, непах, тапухот), г in 389 (йигйе, бигйотам). Is there a rule? (all silent cases follow segol/patach+he+shva within 2 lexemes).

Shva na/nach follows real Hebrew grammar in the Russian text (Sephardi: кедма, гайта, йадха, веарбаа) - not "after long vowel = na". Needs the core engine's syllabifier; the table in vowels.shva-na gives the empirical per-context rates to validate against.

Capitalisation of אֲדֹנָי (lower) vs the tetragrammaton (Адонай): only 16 tokens in torah; zohar/tanya/rambam show no lower-case Адонай but their aligned tokens were lower-cased by the alignment script - re-verify on raw text before encoding.

Not attested at all in the data (profile A): geresh letters (ג׳ ז׳ צ׳ -> дж ж ч), ח/כ with dagesh, Aramaic-only vowel patterns beyond Zohar, rafe marks, yod+qamatz+aleph words (חִיָּיא gave хиййай), apostrophes. Decide manually.
Hebrew abbreviations with geresh/gershayim (ז"ל, שו"ת, בס"ד, ע"ג) are written za"l/бс"д in B and expanded or dropped in A - no verified rule.
Numbers/gematria letters: A converts to arabic digits (ג׳ -> 3, כב -> 22) in references; unclear for other uses.
Capitalised book/part references in Zohar/Tanya/Rambam are translated names (Вайикра, Танйа) rather than rule-based transliteration - exclude from the engine.
Aleph/ayin with a vowel after another vowel (hiatus) is never separated (йааков, беирато): confirmed 99.6-99.8%, but a few B words carry apostrophes - no rule.
